lessons.title: Getting started with a computer
lessons.html:
The parts of a computer

Computers are used in agriculture and food processing for records, stock control, payroll, email, reports and machine control. Operating a computer confidently is a basic workplace skill.

Hardware

  • Input devices: keyboard, mouse or touchpad, scanner, barcode reader, webcam.
  • Processing: the processor (CPU) and memory (RAM) inside the computer.
  • Storage: hard drive or solid-state drive, USB flash drives, cloud storage.
  • Output devices: monitor, printer, speakers.

Software

  • Operating system: the main program that runs the computer, such as Windows, macOS or Linux.
  • Applications: programs for specific tasks: word processor, spreadsheet, email, web browser, farm or abattoir management systems.

Starting up and shutting down

  1. Check that cables are connected and the power outlet is safe.
  2. Press the power button and wait for the login screen.
  3. Log in with your own username and password.
  4. When finished, save your work, close programs and choose Shut down from the start menu. Do not just switch off at the wall; this can damage files.
  5. Lock the screen (on Windows: Windows key + L) when you leave the desk even for a short time.

The desktop

The desktop shows icons, the taskbar or dock, and the start menu. Windows can be opened, minimised, maximised, moved, resized and closed. Use the taskbar or Alt + Tab to switch between open programs.

Using the mouse and keyboard

  • Single click to select, double click to open, right click for a menu of options, drag to move items.
  • Useful shortcuts: Ctrl + C (copy), Ctrl + V (paste), Ctrl + X (cut), Ctrl + Z (undo), Ctrl + S (save), Ctrl + P (print).

lessons.title: Files, folders and printing
lessons.html:
Managing files

A file is a saved document, spreadsheet, picture or other item. A folder holds files and other folders. Good file management means you and others can find work quickly.

Good practice

  • Create a clear folder structure, for example: Quality > Temperature logs > 2026.
  • Use meaningful file names with dates, for example "Chiller log 2026-10-18".
  • Avoid saving everything on the desktop.
  • Know the file extensions: .docx (Word), .xlsx (Excel), .pdf (PDF), .jpg (picture).

Common file tasks

  • Create a new folder: right click, New, Folder.
  • Rename: right click, Rename.
  • Copy keeps the original and makes a second copy; move takes it to a new place.
  • Delete sends it to the Recycle Bin, from where it can be restored until the bin is emptied.
  • Search for a file by name using the search box.

Saving and backups

  • Use Save As the first time to choose the name and folder; then Save often.
  • Back up important files to a network drive, an external drive or approved cloud storage. A computer can break or be stolen.

Printing

  1. Open the file and choose Print (Ctrl + P).
  2. Select the correct printer.
  3. Check the preview, number of copies, page range and orientation.
  4. Print only what you need to save paper and ink.
  5. If the printer jams, follow the instructions on its screen. Switch it off before reaching inside, and be careful of hot parts.

Word processing basics

In a word processor you can type, edit, format (bold, font size, alignment), add bullet lists and tables, check spelling and save documents such as reports and letters.

lessons.title: Email, internet, security and health
lessons.html:
Communicating and finding information

Email

  • Fill in To, Subject and the message. Use Cc to keep others informed.
  • Write a clear subject line, greeting, short message and your name.
  • Attach files using the paperclip icon; check the right file is attached.
  • Reply only to those who need it; use Reply All carefully.
  • Be polite and professional; work email may be read by others.

Internet

  • Use a web browser to search for information. Check that sources are reliable, for example government departments and recognised organisations.
  • Do not download programs unless IT allows it.

Security

  • Use strong passwords: long, with letters, numbers and symbols. Never share your password or write it on the screen.
  • Watch for phishing: emails or messages pretending to be from a bank or supplier, asking you to click a link or give passwords or banking details. Do not click; report it.
  • Do not open attachments from unknown senders.
  • Keep antivirus and updates running.
  • Protect personal information of workers and customers as required by POPIA (Act 4 of 2013).

Health and care of equipment

  • Sit with your back supported, feet flat, screen at eye level about an arm's length away.
  • Take short breaks and look away from the screen regularly to rest your eyes.
  • Keep drinks away from the keyboard.
  • Do not overload plugs or use damaged cables.
  • Clean screens and keyboards with suitable products while the computer is off.

Key points

  • Hardware includes input, processing, storage and output devices; software includes the operating system and applications.
  • Shut down properly and lock the screen when you leave.
  • Use clear folders and file names, save often and back up.
  • Never share passwords and do not click suspicious links.
  • Sit correctly and take breaks to protect your health.

Switching off the computer at the wall is the correct way to shut it down.
Backups protect important files if a computer breaks or is stolen.
